content.comment_body: I need assistance. I have created an hour counter in VM type with data format Dword at address 0, and I want to display it on an HMI from another manufacturer. Using an NAI, I can only select VW, which displays different data. How can I instruct the NAI to use VD and show the true hour counter value? Also, my analog amplifier reports up to 32767, and then the values go negative. I need to show an hour meter of 83000 hours. Any help is appreciated. [user_name]

Welcome to the forum. The NAI module is limited to transmitting only integer values within the range of -32,768 to 32,767, which applies to all analog functions including the amplifier. Does your HMI support displaying Dint values? You haven't mentioned the specific HMI model.
The HMI model is BRAINCHILD - TYPE: 750.
I'm not familiar with the Brainchild 750 HMI. In [product_name], VD refers to DInt, a 32-bit integer format. How is the data from Brainchild read—are you using it as a Vx value or as a DB1 value?

analysis.insight_summary: The user is encountering difficulties in transferring an hour counter value from a [company_name] controller to a third-party HMI. The main issue is that the communication interface only allows integer values within a limited range, causing incorrect display for large hour readings. Integration challenges stem from mismatched data types and the numeric limits of the interface, which especially affect higher counter values.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants the hour counter value from the [company_name] device to be accurately sent and shown on the external HMI, even for high values, without any data discrepancies or conversion issues.
